AI enhancements/advancedVideoRendererSer.module_purpose: Orchestrates AI video rendering through the MaxCore AI server. It generates hook/body/CTA content and sentiment, submits a video job (sync or polled), downloads the result with magic-byte validation into a local cache or a proxy, and overlays text and optional voiceover with local FFmpeg. It also offers a photorealistic path (MaxCore image, Ken Burns zoom, text composite, with a gradient fallback) and a scene-based FFmpeg assembly fallback. Public exports are renderVideo, fetchPhotorealisticImage and maxcoreVideoUrlStore.

It lets the owner register offline agents, create pending tasks, store owner-authored memories, run or retry tasks, and run a read-only knowledge search. It reports degraded states honestly and does not claim completion that the server has not verified.

It defines a typed catalogue of settings outcomes (profile, security, notifications, privacy, connected accounts, API keys), each with a title, description, icon, toast variant and category. It exposes three hooks: one that shows outcome toasts and tracks per-key processing state, one that tracks per-button loading state, and one that does client-side validation for username, email, bio and website fields.

symbols.intent: Hook that lets settings screens announce the result of an action. It looks up a canned title, description and variant from outcomeConfigs and shows a toast. It keeps a short history of recent outcomes and a keyed 'processing' flag map for in-flight operations.

symbols.outputs: Object { showOutcome, recentOutcomes: SettingsOutcome[], setProcessing, getProcessing, outcomeConfigs }. getProcessing returns a boolean and defaults to false.
symbols.side_effects: showOutcome calls useToast().toast and updates React state (recentOutcomes). setProcessing updates state.
symbols.invariants: recentOutcomes is newest-first and capped at 10 entries (prev.slice(0, 9) plus the new one). Every OutcomeType has an entry in outcomeConfigs, enforced by Record<OutcomeType, OutcomeConfig>. The config icon is never passed to the toast, so it is unused here and presumably meant for other consumers. If an unknown type is passed at runtime, config is undefined and showOutcome throws.

symbols.intent: Hook with client-side validators for settings profile fields (username, email, bio, website). Errors are stored in a shared error map, and each validator also returns its own result so callers can use it immediately.
symbols.inputs: No arguments. validateUsername(string), validateEmail(string), validateBio(string) and validateWebsite(string) each take the raw field value. clearError(field) and clearAllErrors() take a field name or nothing.
symbols.outputs: { errors, validateUsername, validateEmail, validateBio, validateWebsite, clearError, clearAllErrors }. Each validator returns { isValid, errors } containing only that call's errors.

Website is optional but must match a URL regex if present. (2) The messages say 'less than 30' and 'less than 500', but the checks allow exactly 30 and 500. (3) The website regex is restrictive: its TLD part is limited to 2-6 letters or dots, and it rejects ports and query strings.
symbols.evidence: L516-609. Validators are implemented with regexes and state merging. No callers appear in the inventory.

client/src/hooks/useBatchAction.ts.module_purpose: React hooks for running bulk operations against `/api/batch/{resource}/{action}`. The core `useBatchAction` hook manages the confirm, execute, progress, result and retry lifecycle, shows toasts, and invalidates React Query caches. A strict response validator, `parseBatchResultResponse`, checks the server payload. Five domain wrappers (distribution, social, marketplace, files, analytics) preconfigure resource, action, messages and query keys.

symbols.intent: Parse and strictly validate a batch endpoint's JSON response against the IDs that were requested, returning a typed BatchResult. It throws if the payload is malformed, the counts are inconsistent, or the results reference IDs that were not requested.
symbols.inputs: response: fetch Response with a JSON body; expectedIds: string[] of the IDs sent in the request.
symbols.outputs: Promise<BatchResult> with success, failed, the three totals, and optional downloadUrl, exportId and comparisonData. Rejects with Error('Batch operation returned an invalid response') or Error('...results for unexpected items').
symbols.side_effects: Consumes the response body via response.json(). No other side effects.
symbols.invariants: totalRequested equals expectedIds.length. totalSucceeded and totalFailed equal the array lengths. success.length + failed.length equals expectedIds.length. Every returned ID is in the requested set. downloadUrl may be null, but exportId may not be null (slight asymmetry).
symbols.evidence: L88-151. The inventory's 'stub=None' is consistent with a full body. Used by execute() at `parseBatchResultResponse(response, ids)`.

symbols.intent: Core hook for a bulk operation. It POSTs (PUT for update) `{ids, data}` to `/api/batch/<resource>/<action>`, tracks status and progress (simulated by a timer when enabled), sets the result, error and status (completed, partial or failed), shows toasts, calls the callbacks, and invalidates the configured query keys. It also exposes confirm, cancel, reset and retryFailed.
symbols.inputs: options: {onSuccess, onError, onProgress, simulateProgress=true}. execute takes a BatchActionConfig {resource, action, ids, data, messages, invalidateQueries}.
symbols.outputs: UseBatchActionReturn: status, progress, result, error, execute, confirm, cancel, reset, retryFailed, isProcessing, isComplete, pendingConfig.
symbols.side_effects: Network request through apiRequest. setInterval timers for the progress simulation. Toasts. React Query invalidation. State updates. Calls the user callbacks.
symbols.invariants: Progress percentage is derived from current/total. The simulated progress never reaches total until the request completes. onSuccess fires for completed and partial outcomes, but not for an all-failed or thrown outcome. Queries are invalidated only when the response is parsed, not when the request throws.
symbols.missing: (1) retryFailed is effectively broken: execute() sets pendingConfig to null on completion, and execute never sets it otherwise, so retryFailed always returns null. (2) The AbortController is created but its signal is never passed to apiRequest, so cancel() does not abort the request. (3) Nothing runs the confirmed pendingConfig, so the caller must invoke execute itself after confirm. (4) A second execute call may leak the previous progress interval. (5) downloadUrl and exportId are returned but not acted on.
symbols.evidence: L153-387. `setPendingConfig(null)` in execute's success path. `abortControllerRef.current = new AbortController()` with no signal use. retryFailed's guard `!pendingConfig`. The inventory's 'stub=empty' reflects only the signature lines L153-154; the body is fully implemented.

client/src/hooks/useBatchActions.ts.module_purpose: React hook module for client-side bulk operations (delete, update, export, submit, schedule, and so on) on resources such as releases, tracks, posts, beats and analytics. The core hook, useBatchActions, runs a confirm/execute/cancel/retry state machine. It calls POST/PUT /api/batch/{resource}/{action}, validates the server response strictly, and reports progress either simulated or polled from a job endpoint. It also raises toasts and invalidates React Query caches. Thin domain wrappers pre-bind resource, action, messages and cache keys. Legacy hooks are re-exported from ./useBatchAction.

symbols.intent: Parse and strictly validate the JSON body of a batch-action response so the UI only handles a consistent BatchResult. The counts must match the requested IDs, and every returned ID must be one that was requested.
symbols.inputs: response: fetch Response; expectedIds: string[] of IDs sent in the request.
symbols.outputs: Promise<BatchResult> with success, failed, totals, and optional downloadUrl, exportId, comparisonData and jobId. Non-string optional fields are normalized to undefined.
symbols.side_effects: Consumes the response body via response.json(). Throws Error('Batch operation returned an invalid response') or '...results for unexpected items' on a bad shape.
symbols.invariants: success and failed are well-typed arrays; totalRequested equals expectedIds.length; totalSucceeded and totalFailed equal the array lengths; success plus failed covers expectedIds.length; all IDs belong to the requested set. It does not check for duplicate IDs or that the two lists are disjoint.
symbols.evidence: L110-173; called from execute() in the same file. The inventory's callers=[] only reflects cross-file callers.

symbols.intent: Parse and validate the response from the batch job progress endpoint, checking it is for the expected job and is internally consistent.
symbols.outputs: Promise<BatchJobProgressResponse>, which is the payload cast after validation.
symbols.side_effects: Reads the response body. Throws Error('Batch progress returned an invalid response') on any violation.
symbols.invariants: jobId matches. status is one of processing, completed or failed. The numeric fields are finite and non-negative. processed <= total. success + failed <= processed, and for a terminal status success + failed == processed. failures is an array of {id, error}.
symbols.evidence: L175-220; used by pollJobProgress in useBatchActions.

symbols.intent: Core hook managing the lifecycle of a batch operation. It supports a confirm step, execution against /api/batch/{resource}/{action}, simulated or job-polled progress, toasts, query invalidation, cancel, reset and retry of failed items.
symbols.inputs: options: onSuccess, onError, onProgress, simulateProgress (default true), pollProgressInterval (default 1000 ms).
symbols.outputs: Object with status, progress, result, error, execute, confirm, cancel, reset, retryFailed, isProcessing, isComplete and pendingConfig.
symbols.side_effects: Sets React state and timers (setInterval). Issues API requests via apiRequest. Shows toasts. Invalidates React Query keys. Calls the callbacks. Creates an AbortController.
symbols.invariants: Status moves idle -> confirming -> processing -> completed, partial, failed or cancelled. Progress percentage is derived from current/total. There are known defects. (1) In useJobProgress mode, pollJobProgress only starts a setInterval and returns immediately. execute therefore resolves, and sets result and clears pendingConfig, before the job finishes. The job-mode path returns early, so onSuccess, the toasts and invalidateQueries never run. (2) The AbortController is never passed to apiRequest, so cancel() does not abort the request. (3) pendingConfig is cleared on completion, so retryFailed() returns null after any finished run. (4) There is no unmount cleanup for the intervals. (5) onProgress is called inside a setState updater, so it is a side effect in a pure function.
